query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: In YBa2Cu3O7−δ thin films, moderate substitution of calcium at the yttrium site will increase the critical current density compared to undoped samples.
generation.material_initial_state: Undoped YBa2Cu3O7−δ thin films with oxygen loading near the optimal doping level and standard critical current properties
generation.intervention: Partial replacement (5–15%) of Y with Ca in YBa2Cu3O7−δ
generation.conditions: Thin-film synthesis under controlled oxygen pressure to maintain near-optimal oxygen content and uniform Ca distribution
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and modified hole doping resulting from the atomic substitution of Ca
generation.mechanism: Ca doping adjusts carrier concentration and lattice parameters, supporting enhanced superconducting coupling
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable (e.g., 10–30%) increase in critical current density at 77 K under zero external magnetic field, relative to undoped YBa2Cu3O7−δ
generation.baseline: Undoped YBa2Cu3O7−δ thin films with nominal critical current values for this cuprate family
generation.boundary: At higher substitution levels (e.g., ≥25% Ca), structural instabilities or phase changes may suppress superconducting performance
generation.uncertainty: No direct data in the provided evidence confirms the exact doping level for maximal current increase or the upper doping limit before degradation sets in

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate a series of YBa2–xCaxCu3O7–δ thin films with x ranging from 0 to 0.3 and measure their critical current density at 77 K in zero field
measurements: Critical current density measurements under standardized conditions
X-ray diffraction to assess phase changes and lattice parameters
Chemical analysis to verify Ca content and oxygen stoichiometry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If increasing Ca content in YBa2–xCaxCu3O7–δ does not correlate with a distinct rise in critical current density (within the predicted range), or if no downturn is observed at higher doping levels, the hypothesis is falsified.
